Redundant second line of defence: lock_blobs builds a BTreeMap, so the arrays bound to the statement are already ascending and the SQL ORDER BY cannot change the lock order for any reachable input. The ascending-order rule itself is killed by the forced-crossing controls in pg_mailbox_concurrency (unordered_blob_locks knob deadlocks) and by mutation D09 not being reachable otherwise.

The sibling D11 (list members, where no trigger pre-empts the unique index) is killed.

Redundant by design: the orphan phase re-checks row absence with blob_row_exists immediately before deleting each file, so an empty shard listing cannot make GC delete a referenced blob (it only makes the orphan sweep skip rows); the file of a referenced blob is protected twice. The row-deleting half of GC is judged by R07 and the gc suites.
